http://www.jpost.com/israel-news/crime-i.text: Police arrested and charged a 28-year-old Kiryat Ata man on Sunday over his alleged involvement in last week's attempted arson at a Haifa Japanika branch.They said the case is linked to a broader wave of grenade and shooting attacks on restaurants in the center of the country. His remand was extended until Monday.Four others have been arrested over their suspected involvement in the attacks on Japanika branches, including Musli crime family boss Yossi Musli, an 18-year-old, and two men in their 30s.In the span of a few hours on Tuesday, police said there were two grenade explosions, a pipe bomb attack, and an attempted arson. Three of the incidents targeted Japanika branches, owned by businessman and Beitar Jerusalem owner Barak Abramov. Later, police responded to a shooting incident at the Herzliya branch.Perpetrators used a stolen IDF grenade during the Netanya attack.Jarushi crime family associate turns himself inAlso on Sunday, Jarushi crime family associate Issa Alohuah turned himself in to the police at 3 a.m. before his official arrest on suspicion of conspiracy to commit a crime.Police requested an extension of Alohuah's detention by six days after he was brought to the Rishon Lezion Magistrate's Court, but the court granted only a three-day extension.Japanika probe goes international as FBI, Romanian police join investigationThe investigation into the attacks on Japanika has expanded internationally, with the FBI and Romanian police now involved, N12 reported on Friday.Channel 12 legal analyst Guy Peleg said authorities believe that Eran Haya, the head of a crime organization who is being held in Brooklyn, is connected to the matter.“The FBI raided his cell and found cellphones that he had 'stashed' there,” he said.“The Romanian security service questioned Yossi Musli's brother, Eli Musli, based on materials transferred by Israel Police. The Romanian authorities made it clear to Musli that if this continues, they will shut down the businesses in Romania. There will be results and achievements in this case.”Jerusalem Post Staff, Goldie Katz, Esther Davis, and Hodaya Ran contributed to this report.

Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/AP View image in fullscreen Andy Burnham and Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv before their bilateral meeting on Monday, where Burnham reiterated the UK’s ‘steadfast’ support. Photograph: Henry Nicholls/AFP/AP Andy Burnham Burnham plans trip to New York as Ukraine pleads for US-made missiles UK prime minister ‘likely’ to attend UN general assembly, after meeting Zelenskyy and saying supply problem is fixable Europe live – latest updates Peter Walker Senior political correspondent Tue 25 Aug 2026 04.27 EDT First published on Tue 25 Aug 2026 03.03 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Andy Burnham has said he is likely to attend the UN general assembly in New York next month, a chance for the new prime minister to meet a host of world leaders. While Downing Street said the plans were not definite, the prime minister told Bloomberg in an interview: “I’m looking forward to going to New York in September.” Speaking in Kyiv after a meeting with the Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , Burnham went on: “I’ve not fully confirmed the details yet but it’s likely I will go, particularly after today’s discussion. Leaving today, I’m quite clear what I need to do in the next few weeks.” If it did take place, it would be Burnham’s first visit to the US since taking office, and could potentially provide an opportunity for a face-to-face meeting with Donald Trump. Dozens of world leaders gather annually for the general assembly. This year’s meeting takes place from 22-28 September, which could be logistically tricky for Burnham given Labour’s annual conference begins in Liverpool on 27 September. Attending would give Burnham the opportunity to meet a number of other world leaders at once, even if bilateral talks tend to be brief amid the frenetic schedule of the gathering. Burnham’s policy background is predominantly domestic, and since entering No 10 he has had to rapidly develop a foreign policy – thus far very similar to that of Keir Starmer – and get to know world leaders. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to First Edition Our morning email breaks down the key stories of the day, telling you what’s happening and why it matters after newsletter promotion Burnham’s visit to Kyiv marks a renewal of badly needed support for Ukraine Read more In Kyiv on Monday, for his first official overseas trip since becoming prime minister in July, Burnham laid a wreath for Ukraine’s Independence Day, joining a number of other European leaders, including the European council president, António Costa. He also used the trip to announce that the UK government would allow the European defence company MBDA to declassify information about UK-made components of the Anglo-French Storm Shadow/Scalp missiles to help Ukraine build its own version. During his meeting with Zelenskyy, Burnham said there would be “no change in the UK’s steadfast support” for Kyiv . 8:57 Burnham hands secret missile technology to Ukraine in first foreign trip - The Latest He also urged Ukraine’s allies to send more Patriot missiles to Kyiv as Ukraine struggles under continued Russian bombardment, and co-chaired his first coalition of the willing meeting, where he said the group was doing “everything we can” to “dig into our own stocks and help others dig into their stocks”. Zelenskyy has pleaded for more US-made interceptor missiles in recent months as Kyiv’s stocks have diminished. Supplies of Patriots have been diverted to the Middle East since the outbreak of the US’s war against Iran, with Ukraine receiving significantly fewer missiles this year than in previous years. During the interview with Bloomberg, Burnham said he felt “really confident” the weaponry problem was fixable, but added: “There are other players who could help in the mix who we have influence with. It’s probably going to be a solution that involves a lot of layers and a lot of negotiation.” Russia has sought to capitalise on the shortage by increasing its ballistic missile strikes, killing at least 23 people and wounding more than 100 in the past three days. Russia has threatened unspecified potential retaliation against the UK for what Moscow says is increased involvement in the conflict. https://www.dw.com/en/cuban-dance-teache.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MQHq Oemis Romagoza Durruthy teaches Latin dance in northern Russia Image: vk.ru Advertisement On social media platforms , the man called himself "Adrian" or "Dios," meaning "God” in Spanish. In 2024, accounts linked to the man posted job ads on Telegram . "Work as a photographer," one offered in Russian in a chat about opportunities in Poland. "To those interested in applying, send resume, phone number and passport," another advertised in a group for Cuban expatriates in Russia . "Looking for people with military experience in monitoring, intelligence, logistics and tactical maneuvers," one said in Spanish in a group for Latinos, promising $1,500 (about €1,300) plus a bonus for each operation completed. Dios lured multiple people into carrying out sabotage for Russia in at least four EU countries, an investigation by DW and three other European broadcasters has found. Most of the recruits came from Spanish-speaking countries. For months, DW and its partners conducted dozens of interviews with security officials and people close to the suspects. We pieced together classified court documents, official statements, social media posts and leaked data to find out who Dios is and reconstruct how he built a network of saboteurs to commit arson attacks across Europe. Not all of them completed their tasks. Recruiting vulnerable people One of the people Dios recruited was Luis Alfonso Murillo Diosa, who was 34 years old at the time. Originally from Caicedo, a rural town in western Colombia known for its mountainous landscapes and its crops, Murillo was raised in a family of coffee farmers. But several years of poor harvests pushed the business into debt, according to someone close to the family. Murillo spent six years in the Colombian army. According to court documents, he left in 2015. He then hopped between jobs like many ex-soldiers, juggling barista courses, stints as a bodyguard and his family's coffee business. In early 2024, Murillo decided to enlist in the Ukrainian army, where foreign fighters can earn a few thousand euros a month when deployed to the front line, court documents show. Looking for information about the process, he joined a Facebook group for Latin Americans seeking to fight in Ukraine . That's when he was contacted by Dios. "It's often vulnerable people who are being targeted,” said Daniela Richterova, an associate professor in Intelligence Studies at King's College London. "Vulnerable people who need money and are willing to travel for money and are willing to not ask many questions about the purpose of what they're carrying out." Murillo said he sought to join the Ukrainian army, not work for Russia Image: Facebook Arrested for attempted sabotage In a private Facebook message, Dios introduced himself as a member of a "special group," and asked Murillo to work with him on "special missions" in Europe instead of going to Ukraine, according to classified court documents reviewed by DW. Murillo took the offer, and Dios organized everything remotely: flight tickets, accommodation, ground transport. They never met in person. Once Murillo reached Bucharest in July 2024, Dios sent him a satellite image with a recycling facility and an oil well marked. Murillo was supposed to take photos and videos of the locations — and later start a fire. However, he was detained while walking near the recycling facility one night after taking photos. According to court records, Murillo told investigators that he never intended to commit arson. He said he was trying to get to Europe to reach Ukraine, and didn't know for whom he was working. In 2025, Murillo was sentenced to six years in prison for attempted sabotage. Russia's 'disposable agents' DW and its partners have confirmed that Murillo was one of at least a dozen people recruited by Dios for acts of sabotage across Europe. Such recruits are frequently referred to as "disposable agents": people often hired online who at times don't even know the identities of their employers or the real aim of their assignments. The Kremlin has increasingly used disposable agents after EU governments expelled scores of Russian diplomats suspected of espionage and disinformation following the 2022 invasion of Ukraine , the conflict researcher Keir Giles told DW. "That left a gap in Russia's capability, and it took time for them to find this new means of recruiting random people to carry out sometimes apparently random attacks," said Giles, who has written several books about Russia's military. In 2024 alone, disposable agents burned down a shopping center in Poland , set fire to an Ikea store in Lithuania and delivered incendiary packages that ignited at logistics hubs in several countries . German authorities said throwaway agents, as they are also called, steered a drone with explosives toward a Ukrainian freight plane in Leipzig in August. The 2024 attack on a Warsaw shopping center has been attributed to disposable agents Image: Attila Husejnow/SOPA/IMAGO The suspected perpetrators of such attacks are often not Russian — nor do they have a known prior connection to Russian intelligence services. Many of the people prosecuted have been Ukrainian refugees, low-level criminals or local youths looking to make quick money. "Russia doesn't have to be particularly careful about covering its tracks, because there is no downside to being detected," Giles said. "And, of course, it boosts the idea that Russia wants to project that it is omnipotent, that it can cause damage wherever." Russian arson made in Cuba DW confirmed that, over a span of four months in 2024, Dios instructed his recruits to set fire to two construction-supply businesses in Poland, a bus garage in the Czech Republic, a recycling facility in Romania and equipment destined for Ukraine produced by a company in Lithuania. Lithuanian prosecutors were the only ones to publicly attribute the series of arson attacks to Russia's military intelligence service, known as GRU. They also put a Cuban man living in Russia on an international wanted list. After reviewing classified court documents and dozens of leaked files, DW and its partners were able to confirm that Cuban national Oemis Romagoza Durruthy is the man behind the alias Dios. Lithuanian prosecution has added Oemis Romagoza Durruthy to an international wanted list Image: LRT Born in Camaguey, Cuba's third-largest city, Romagoza has lived in Russia for at least seven years. A Latin dance teacher in the northern Russian city of Petrozavodsk, Romagoza is listed as a contact person on the social media channels of a local dance studio, Made in Cuba. In dozens of online videos of his dance classes, he shows off his salsa, bachata and kizomba steps. Romagoza married a Russian woman in 2022 and later obtained Russian citizenship. A series of wedding photos DW found on social media show the couple posing next to a grand piano. Other pictures show them with their two children. DW was unable to determine when and how he came to work on behalf of Russia's secret services. Leaked data indicate that Romagoza might have run into financial trouble. In 2023, he borrowed money from several credit lenders. In one of the entries, he listed a supermarket chain as his employer. A few months later, Romagoza joined several Facebook groups of Latin Americans looking for work in Poland or seeking to fight for Ukraine. Around the same time, Dios started posting job offers on Telegram. Born in Cuba, Romagoza has lived in Russia for at least seven years Image: Instagram Sabotage continues in EU It is unclear whether Dios continued recruiting people or directed more attacks after September 2024. But Russia's relentless sabotage campaign across Europe hasn't stopped. In August alone, Estonia arrested two suspects for an arson attack targeting a company that supplies unmanned military vehicles to Ukraine, and Poland reported fires at two other facilities where components for drones and helicopters are manufactured . Authorities in both countries suspect that Russia is behind the plots. "It seems like there are still people out there who are either naive enough or are really hungry for money and motivated by monetary rewards for these kinds of activities," said Richterova, whose research focuses on Russian intelligence. At least nine of the disposable agents Romagoza recruited have been caught. Two are serving sentences of six to eight years for attempted sabotage or terrorism. Others are currently awaiting trial. Meanwhile, European authorities are still after Romagoza, who might still be in Russia. In April, the Made in Cuba studio posted a video of him teaching a salsa class. Romagoza is seen facing the mirror, leading a group of women who follow his steps and his commands. "Because that is what I am. In heaven, I am the chief," sings the Cuban salsa tune playing in the background. Around the same time the Latin dance studio posted the video, Romagoza joined at least two more Facebook groups for Latin Americans looking for work in Poland. Oemis Romagoza Durruthy did not reply to requests for comment. https://www.dw.com/en/india-news-amit-sh.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OtLt Prefer DW on Google Amit Shah called the allegations against the Election Commission 'baseless' [FILE: May 8, 2026] Image: ANI Video Grab Advertisement Skip next section What you need to know What you need to know Union Home Minister Amit Shah challenged opposition leader Rahul Gandhi to debate allegations of electoral irregularities in parliament India successfully launches satellite to boost indigenous GPS alternative German citizen among 2 killed in Bengaluru hotel pool accident Delhi experiences coldest October day in 75 years Here are the top headlines from India on Saturday, October 31: Skip next section Vote theft row: Shah challenges opposition as INDIA bloc prepares major protest 10/31/2026 October 31, 2026 Vote theft row: Shah challenges opposition as INDIA bloc prepares major protest Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Friday challenged opposition leaders Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav to discuss allegations of electoral irregularities in parliament, even as the opposition geared for a major rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar , according to media reports. "I am ready to call a special session of Parliament to discuss vote theft allegations," Shah said, accusing the opposition of making baseless allegations against the Election Commission and staging protests while skirting parliamentary debate. His remarks came as the opposition INDIA bloc prepared to hold a symbolic "public impeachment" of Kumar on Saturday, followed by a major rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on November 1. Around 30 speakers from 21 opposition parties are expected to participate. The opposition is demanding Kumar's resignation over his role in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and the scrapping of the SIR, alleging that the exercise could disenfranchise voters and benefit the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). In a call for the November 1 rally, Rahul Gandhi said "anyone who cares about democracy must come." "The vote is yours . The fight is also yours," the Congress leader wrote on X. Earlier, the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) also threw their weight behind the rally saying the movement would lend its support to any organization fighting for free and fair elections in India , including the opposition alliance. Students cheer during the victory march inside the Jamia Millia University campus after the university administration agreed to restore their student union Image: Sanchit Khanna/Hindustan Times/Sipa USA/picture alliance Edited by: Wesley Rahn https://p.dw.com/p/5OtTt Skip next section Friday was Delhi's coldest October day in 75 years 10/31/2026 October 31, 2026 Friday was Delhi's coldest October day in 75 years Delhi received 61.4 mm rainfall in the 24 hours ending 8.30 am Friday, the IMD said Image: Raj K Raj/Hindustan Times/Sipa USA/picture alliance On Friday, Delhi experienced temperatures more typical of a winter day than an October afternoon. Delhi recorded its lowest October daytime temperature in 75 years on Friday, with a maximum temperature of 20.7 degrees Celsius, which more than 10 degrees below normal, PTI news agency reported, citing data from the India Meteorological Department (IMD). The low temperature came after two days of persistent rainfall. The maximum temperature at Safdarjung, Delhi's base weather station, was the lowest for October since records began in 1951, the IMD data added. Delhi also recorded its wettest October day in four years, receiving 61.4 mm of rainfall in the 24 hours ending Friday morning. The rainfall also helped clean up air pollution levels, with the Indian capital's notoriously bad Air Quality Index (AQI) improving to a "satisfactory" reading of 60. However, experts say pollution levels could deteriorate to the "poor" category on November 1 and remain poor or very poor over the coming days. Edited by: Wesley Rahn https://p.dw.com/p/5OtRd Skip next section India successfully launches satellite to boost indigenous GPS alternative 10/31/2026 October 31, 2026 India successfully launches satellite to boost indigenous GPS alternative India's space agency successfully launched a navigation satellite on Friday night to strengthen the country's indigenous alternative to GPS. The NVS-03 satellite, the third in Indian Space Research Organisation's (ISRO) next-generation navigation series, was carried into orbit by the "GSLV-F18" rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, located on an island in the Bay of Bengal. According to ISRO the "the GSLV-F18 vehicle placed NVS-03 satellite into a Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit." An earlier statement by the agency said the satellite is "intended to augment the NavIC constellation and support continuity of navigation services." It is designed to provide navigation coverage across India and up to 1,500 kilometers (932 miles) beyond its borders. NavIC is seen as an alternative to the Global Positioning System (GPS) system owned by the United States government and developed to reduce India's dependence on foreign navigation systems. Prime Minister Narendra Modi celebrated the successful launch as a "great accomplishment." Edited by: Wesley Rahn https://p.dw.com/p/5OtOP Skip next section Strait of Hormuz attacks: Two tankers carrying Indians hit by mines in two days 10/31/2026 October 31, 2026 Strait of Hormuz attacks: Two tankers carrying Indians hit by mines in two days The attack on Louise 1 comes amid repeated attacks on commercial shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz [FILE: July 9, 2026] Image: Yoruk Isik/REUTERS An oil tanker carrying 27 Indian seafarers was targeted with limpet mines in the Strait of Hormuz. A small boat attached two mines to the vessel's hull, causing a fire in the engine room, maritime security sources said on Friday. Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said all Indian seafarers aboard the vessel were safe and had sustained no injuries. Sonowal also added that two Indians aboard another tanker that faced a separate attack on October 29 were also safe. The attack on the Panama-flagged Louise 1 occurred on Thursday, around 25 nautical miles (46 km) northeast of Oman's Khasab. The fire was extinguished, the crew was safe and there was no environmental impact, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said. The incident marks the first known successful use of limpet mines against a vessel in the waterway since the US-Iran war began in February. The identity of those behind the attacks was not immediately known. The Strait of Hormuz, a vital chokepoint for oil and gas transport , is seeing attacks on ships at the highest level since the Iran war began, according to US-based think tank Washington Institute for Near East Policy. Incidentally, the Louise 1 was hit earlier with naval drones in the Black Sea by Ukrainian forces over its alleged role in transporting Russian oil and being part of the so-called shadow fleet of tankers deployed by Moscow.
